newsitem.title: USA: Green group wary of Salem nuke plant fire safety.
newsitem.headline: Green group wary of Salem nuke plant fire safety.

text.p: The Union of Concerned Scientists wants the Nuclear Regulatory Commission to change or enforce its rule on fire safety seals before the Salem nuclear plant in New Jersey is allowed to restart, an official with the environmental group said Monday.
NRC staff last week recommended that the Salem plant, run by Public Service Electric and Gas, should be allowed to come out of a two-year outage.

But the Union of Concerned Scientsts said the silicone foam that the plant uses as a fire seal in the holes in walls, floors and ceilings where wires and pipes pass through does not meet existing NRC rules for fire barriers.
The group is urging Democratic Sen. Joseph Biden of Delaware to pressure the NRC to change or enforce its rule requiring the seal material to be non-combustible before the plant restarts.

"We're trying get Biden's office to make the foam issue a restart item for the plant," said David Lochbaum, nuclear safety engineer for the environmental group. "We want the NRC to change the rule before the restart or get the company to apply for an exemption."

While the widely-used foam is considered good enough to prevent fire spreading from one room to another, the material smolders and does not technically meet the NRC requirement for fire barrier penetration seals to be "non-combustible".

The NRC last year proposed to revise its 17-year-old rule to allow silicone foam to be used, but the agency has yet to make the change. Technically, any plant that uses the material is out of compliance with the NRC rule.
In a statement Monday, Rep. Ed Markey Monday slammed the commission's plan to rewrite its rule.

"This decision to relax fire safety requirements will no doubt save nuclear utilities millions of dollars; what it will not do is help to save people's lives in the event of a fire," the Massachusetts Democrat and NRC critic said in a statement.
An NRC official defended the proposal, saying that when the fire regulation was written in 1979 it was intended to bar the use of highly combustible materials, not silicone foam.
"(Silicone foam)'s difficult to ignite and if it does burn, it burns slowly," said Steven West, the NRC's fire protection engineering chief.
In addition to PSE&G, owners of Salem are PECO Energy Co, D elmarva Power & Light Co, and Atlantic Energy Inc.
